base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

revision.description: The diff `new_revision` the client reviewed. A changed revision refuses with `stale_revision`.

oneOf.description: Move one issue of a board to a column and a place in that column. The host moves the issue, then tells the owner with a `move` event.

index.description: The place in the column after the move: 0 is the top. A larger number puts the issue at the bottom.

oneOf.description: Ask the owner of a board to make, change or delete an issue. Without `item_id`, the owner makes a new issue from `values`. The owner changes the board; the host changes nothing.

is_removed.description: True asks the owner to delete the issue `item_id`.

base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

item_id.description: The canvas item that a new thread of a canvas belongs to.

body.description: The new draft. Null removes the draft. Blank text removes the draft of a thread without messages, and a new blank thread is not created. On a thread with messages, blank text saves an empty draft: the messages go into the next message of the session without a note.

base_seq.description: The state version the client edited. A newer write to the same node refuses with `conflict`.

revision.description: The diff `new_revision` the client reviewed. A changed revision refuses with `stale_revision`.

input_view.description: Public input View projection. Routing, validation rules and secret-storage flags stay at the host; created_at and origin are engine stamps.

input_origin.description: The session that asks. A form from a subagent session also names its parent: the leader session, which shows the form.

view.description: The view. A stream that asked for `app_opens=summary` gets the summary of an app whose body holds more characters than `x-vis-elide-above-chars` of `patch_event`. A client that has the view at that `seq` keeps its body. Another client reads the app when it shows it.

is_elided.description: True when the stream left out the patch of an app. Only a stream that asked for `app_patches=elided` gets such a frame, and only for a patch whose strings hold more characters than `x-vis-elide-above-chars`. The view changed: a client that shows it reads it again.

last_seq.description: The seq of the view after an elided frame. A frame with a patch has it in the patch.

string_edit.description: One change of a string. At `start`, `delete` UTF-16 code units of the base string go out and `insert` comes in. `start` counts in the base string.

patch_splice.description: A long string of one `set` or `add-node` operation, as edits of a base string. The operation comes without the key. The base is the string that the node has for the key before the operation. For a node that an earlier operation of the frame removed, the base is the string that the node had when the frame started.

op_index.description: The index of the operation in `ops`.

node_id.description: The node that has the key. In an `add-node` operation, it is `node_spec` or a node in its `children`. Absent: the node of the operation.

key.description: The key of the node that the edits give.

base_hash.description: The hash of the base string: `h = 31 * h + unit` for each UTF-16 code unit, kept as a signed 32-bit number. A client whose string has another hash reads the view.

edits.description: In ascending order of `start`, without overlap.

view_delta.description: One published frame of an app, as a read with `since` gives it. A string with more characters than `x-vis-splice-above-chars` comes as a `patch_splice` when the node had a string of that length before. The gateway keeps the newest frames of an app while their strings hold at most `x-vis-chars-kept` characters. It answers the whole view when the frames hold more characters than the view.

patch.description: A `live_patch`. An operation comes without each key that a splice gives.

lane.description: One bar of a timeline. Times are epoch milliseconds. A lane without end still runs, and end is never before start.

badge_item.description: One badge: a short label with an optional tone.

list_item.description: One item of a list: its text, with an optional second line and tone.

chart_series.description: One series of a chart. Value N belongs to category N. A series can be shorter than the categories.

anchor.description: The diff lines that a thread belongs to: the file path, the old or new side and the 1-based line on that side. For a range of lines, start_line is the first line and line is the last line. start_side is the side of the first line when it is not side. The thread shows below the last line.

start_side.description: The side of start_line when the range starts on the other side, as in a change from a removed line to an added line.

start_line.description: The first line of a range. On the same side, it is not after line.

author.description: Who wrote a message. The host sets it from the authenticated caller; a client never sends it.

message.description: One posted message of a thread.

thread.description: A discussion with stable message ids. `draft` is the saved, unsent text of the human. The next message of the session takes each draft and its thread messages, and then the draft is removed. An empty draft adds the messages without a note.

item_id.description: The id of the canvas item that the thread belongs to. Only a thread of a canvas has it.

submission_status.description: The delivery stage of one Send: stored, handed to the owner, in work, answered or failed.

item_id.description: The canvas item of the thread.

submission.description: The host receipt of one Send. The id stays the same for every retry with the same idempotency key.

values.description: The non-secret values of the inputs that the Send collected.

idempotency_key.description: A client key that makes a retried Send return the first submission.

app_attachment.description: The attachment row of an app. Its bytes hold the opening picture; the live view holds the current state.

shortcut_key.description: One key that an app shortcut binds: one printable ASCII character from `!` to `~` (case-sensitive, so `A` is Shift+a) or one named key. Modifiers are never bindable. `Escape` and `Tab` stay with the surface.

shortcut.description: One app shortcut. It sends the `action` id to the owner code, or presses the button or selectable card `node_id` like a click.

label.description: The short text that a surface shows in its shortcut legend.

action.description: The id that the owner code receives in a `shortcut` event.

node_id.description: A button or a selectable card of the app. A surface presses it as a click.

command_icon.description: A picture that a surface can show next to the label of a command or a field, or instead of it in a toolbar. The label stays the accessible name.

reveals.description: The key of another app of the same owner and session. When a person activates the node, the surface shows that app. It waits for the app to open.

categories.description: The label of each position on the horizontal axis.

line_tones.description: Optional tones aligned with lines; null means plain text.

is_dialog.description: True when the group is a dialog. A surface shows it over the view, with its label as the title, only while `is_open` is true. A person closes it with `activate` on the group: the host sets `is_open` to false and then sends the owner the `activate` event.

is_open.description: True while a dialog group shows. Only a dialog takes it.

is_selected.description: The choice that holds now. A menu of a diff toolbar marks it, a view paints the button as one choice of its row, and a press chooses it again.

children.description: The toolbar of the diff. A button is one action. A group of buttons is one menu, and its label names the current choice.

oneOf.description: A picture. With `before`, the surface compares the old picture with the new one.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a person who cannot see it.

before.description: The old picture. Absent means a single picture.

oneOf.description: A 3D picture that the owner describes and every surface draws. x points right, y up and z to the viewer; the camera fits the rectangle from (0, 0) to (width, height) at z = 0.

fov.description: The vertical field of view in degrees. 0 is an orthographic camera.

is_wrapping.description: True when an object that leaves one edge comes back at the other. A surface then eases it the short way.

tick_ms.description: How long a surface eases an object to its new place. 0 jumps.

oneOf.description: A board of issues in columns, as a team plans its work. A person drags an issue to another column or place, opens an issue to read and change it, and makes new issues. The owner chooses which issues the board shows: an app filters and searches them with its own inputs.

group_by.description: The field that puts the issues in rows across the columns. Absent means one row.

is_editable.description: True when a person can move, make, change and delete issues. The owner gets each `move` and `edit` event.

is_selectable.description: True when a person can open an issue. The open issue is the selected issue.

people.description: The people that an issue can name as its assignee.

epics.description: The large pieces of work that an issue can belong to.

oneOf.description: A board of items with arrows between them, which a person can pan and zoom. An item is a card, a shape, a sticky note, a comment, a frame or a text. A surface puts the items in steps: an item goes one step after the last item that it comes from. `column` and `row` put an item in a fixed place.

zoom.description: The scale of the board: 1 shows a card at its full size. 0 or no value fits the focus in the surface.

focus.description: The id of the card that the surface puts in the centre. An empty string or no value shows the whole board. An id that no card has shows the whole board until that card arrives.

is_locked.description: True when a person cannot pan or zoom the board. The owner still moves it with `zoom` and `focus`.

threads.description: The discussions on the items of the board. Each thread names its item with `item_id`, and one item can have more than one thread. A thread whose item the canvas does not hold shows when that item arrives. A removed item takes its threads with it. A thread of a board is smaller than a thread of a diff: it holds at most 50 messages of 4000 characters.

oneOf.description: From `x-vis-fold-at` options on, a client shows the field as one line that opens a list. The client fits the list height to its screen.

public_component.description: A component as the input View projection shows it. Validation rules and secret-storage flags stay at the host.

live_owner.description: Host-stamped Activity invocation and optional persistent history that own a live view.

placement.description: Where a live view shows. `attachment` makes a durable app attachment: it outlives the call that opened it and keeps its state after a restart.

inline.description: Show the app in the chat turn that opened it.

session.description: Where the session apps button opens the app: beside the chat, in the chat area, or not at all.

picture.description: One picture as base64 data. The data holds at most 2 MiB of picture bytes; JSON makes it 4/3 larger. An app always sends `data`; only the picture that the model reads has `bytes` in its place. `x-vis-magic` lists the first bytes of each media type: a picture matches one list, and each entry of that list is hex bytes at an offset. The header may hold at most `x-vis-max-pixels` pixels.

bytes.description: Set by the host in the picture that the model reads: the size of the picture in bytes. The model never reads `data`.

width.description: The picture width in pixels. The host reads it from the picture header; a value from the owner must match.

height.description: The picture height in pixels. The host reads it from the picture header; a value from the owner must match.

log_level.description: How serious one app log entry is.

log_entry.description: One entry of the debug log of an app. The host numbers the entries and stamps the time. A writer may send longer text: the host cuts it by code points. A long `message` keeps its start and ends with `…`. A long `detail` keeps its start and its end, joined by a line with `…`. A blank `detail` is dropped.

at.description: Milliseconds since the epoch when the host took the entry.

source.description: `app` for an entry that the owner wrote; `host` for an entry that Vis wrote, for example a failed callback.

detail.description: More text, for example a stack trace.

app_icon.description: The icon of an app. Clients use the same name for a picture or a terminal mark.

app_scope.description: Who an app belongs to. A `session` app belongs to the session that opened it. A `global` app belongs to no session: only an SDK program opens it, through `POST /v1/apps`.

extension.description: The extension that owns this panel view.

surfaces.description: Where an app shows. The opener declares the defaults. A reader gets the values after the person's settings. Only an app takes surfaces.

icon.description: The icon of this app. Absent means app. Only an app takes an icon.

settings_name.description: The name of the settings of this app. Apps of one owner with the same name share one pair of settings. Absent means the key. Only an app takes a settings name.

settings_key.description: The id prefix of the settings of this app: `<settings_key>_inline` and `<settings_key>_session`. Only an app with a key has them.

scope.description: Who this app belongs to. Absent means `session`. Only an app takes a scope, and a `global` app needs a key.

is_persistent.description: Whether a global app comes back after a gateway restart, as a stale picture until its owner adopts it by key. Absent means true. Only a global app takes it.

is_stale.description: True for the saved picture of an owned view after a gateway restart, until its extension loads again.

is_reconnectable.description: True for a stale app that gets its owner back when a client sends the `connect` action.

is_archived.description: True when the owner archived this app. It keeps its state and leaves the default lists.

is_closed.description: True when the owner closed this app. It keeps its last state and takes no more actions.

shortcuts.description: The keyboard shortcuts of an app, with unique keys. Only an app takes shortcuts.

agent_note.description: The app state that the model reads with the next user message. Only an app takes a note.

submissions.description: The newest Send receipts of an app, oldest first.

log.description: The newest debug log entries of an app, oldest first. Only an app takes a log.

draft_entry.description: One saved thread draft of an app. `quote` holds the messages of the thread, such as a finding of a check.

item_id.description: The canvas item of the thread.

live_view_summary.description: An app in a list that asked for `summary=true`, or in a `view.open` event of a stream that asked for `app_opens=summary`: the live view of the app without its body. The properties with the schema `false` are the keys that a summary leaves out. Read the view to get them.

drafts.description: The saved thread drafts of the app, which the composer shows. The summary leaves this out when the app has no draft.

x-vis-patch-targets.description: The node types that each node op takes, and the op keys that each node type takes in that op. The first key of an append is the collection of the node. Every host refuses an op outside this table with the op_target or op_key rule, before it applies the op.

detail.description: Blank text clears the status' detail; a declaration omits it instead.

tone.description: Semantic styling for every line in this append; log nodes only.

item_ids.description: The ids of the things to remove. For a canvas, an id names an item or a thread, and a removed item takes its threads with it.

oneOf.description: Replace every row of a table, or every issue of a board, at once. Selected ids whose rows or issues are gone are dropped.

thread.description: To change only the resolution of an existing thread, give its id and is_resolved without messages.

shortcuts.description: The new shortcut list. It replaces the old list, and an empty list removes every shortcut.

text.description: The new note for the model. It replaces the old note, and a blank text removes the note.

message.description: The message, up to 4 times the entry bound. The host first redacts secrets and then cuts the text to the entry bound, so a cut never splits a labelled secret.

detail.description: More text, for example a stack trace, up to 4 times the entry bound. The host first redacts secrets and then cuts the text to the entry bound.

at.description: Set by the host: the time of the entry.

source.description: Set by the host: `app` for an owner patch, `host` for an entry of Vis.

input_result.description: Public input close receipt. Submitted values and secret handles are returned only to the waiting extension, never to the event stream.

live_close.description: Public live close receipt. SSE may omit the already-streamed view; consumers retain the picture assembled from open and patch events. Journal polling may include the settled view.

datetime_mode.description: What a datetime field asks for. The value is local time without a zone: `YYYY-MM-DD` for date, `HH:MM` for time and `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` for datetime.

datetime_text.description: A date, a time or both. A field takes only the form of its mode.

group_direction.description: How a group arranges its children. A `toolbar` puts compact children on one line that wraps: a text or choice input shows its label only as its accessible name, and a checkbox keeps its label next to the box. A surface shows the first toolbar at the top level of an app in the band of the app. The other toolbars stay in their places.

scene_builtin_mesh.description: A mesh that every scene knows without a declaration. Each vertex lies inside the unit cube; each face is a triangle in counter-clockwise order seen from outside. Both surfaces read these arrays, so a shape looks the same on every screen.

scene_mesh.description: A mesh that one scene declares: triangles in counter-clockwise order seen from outside, so a surface can drop the back faces.

scene_object.description: One object of a scene: a mesh with a place, a turn, a size and a colour.

mesh.description: A built-in mesh name or the id of a mesh that the scene declares.

rx.description: Rotation about the x axis in degrees. A surface turns about x, then y, then z.

is_emissive.description: True paints the full colour without light, as a glow.

scene_object_change.description: A change of one scene object. Keys that it leaves out keep their value. A new id needs a `mesh`.

mesh.description: A built-in mesh name or the id of a mesh that the scene declares.

rx.description: Rotation about the x axis in degrees. A surface turns about x, then y, then z.

is_emissive.description: True paints the full colour without light, as a glow.

canvas_card.description: One item of a canvas. An append with the id of an item replaces that whole item.

text.description: The body of the item in Markdown. Each surface renders it as it renders a message of the session: headings, lists, task lists, tables, code blocks, quotes, and links.

column.description: The step of the card in the flow. A wide surface puts the steps from left to right and a narrow surface puts them from top to bottom. Without it, the card goes one step after the last card that it comes from.

row.description: The place of the card among the cards of its step. Without it, a surface puts the card near the cards that it comes from, and cards with the same place keep the order of the canvas.

shape.description: The outline of an item of kind `shape`. Other kinds ignore it.

color.description: The colour of the border, the fill and the icon. Without it, the item has the neutral colour of its tone.

border.description: The line of the border. `none` draws no border.

caption.description: A short line under the item, outside its border.

progress.description: The part of the work that is done, from 0 to 1. A surface shows a bar in the item.

parent.description: The id of the item of kind `frame` that holds this item. An item whose parent the canvas does not hold, or whose parent is not a frame, stands on the board itself. A frame can hold frames, to a depth of 4. An item under a deeper frame stands on the board itself.

edges.description: The arrows that end at this card. Each arrow must start at a different item.

canvas_edge.description: An arrow to the card that holds it. An arrow from a card that the canvas does not hold shows when that card arrives.

from.description: The id of the card where the arrow starts.

is_active.description: True when work moves along the arrow now. A surface animates it.

line.description: The line of the arrow. `none` draws nothing: the arrow only orders the cards.

start_mark.description: The mark at the card where the arrow starts.

end_mark.description: The mark at the card where the arrow ends.

animation.description: How a surface animates the arrow while `is_active` is true. The default is `flow`.

canvas_kind.description: What an item of a canvas is. `card` has a title line, text, badges and a picture. `shape` has its title in the middle of an outline. `note` is a sticky note. `frame` is a titled area that holds other items. `text` is a title and text with no border, such as a heading on the board.

canvas_color.description: A colour by name. Each surface has its own shade of the colour for a light and a dark theme.

canvas_fill.description: How much of the colour fills the item: `none` leaves it clear, `soft` tints it and `solid` paints it.

canvas_animation.description: A motion that draws the eye to the item. A surface stops it for a person who asks for reduced motion.

canvas_picture.description: A picture in an item, as base64 data. It follows the rules of `picture` and counts in the picture bytes of the view.

alt.description: What the picture shows, for a person who cannot see it.

fit.description: `cover` fills the picture area and cuts the edges. `contain` shows the whole picture.

canvas_media.description: A video or a sound in an item, by its web address. A surface loads nothing until the person starts it.

alt.description: What the video or the sound holds, for a person who cannot play it.

canvas_route.description: The path of an arrow. An elbow has only lines at right angles, and it goes around the items and the other arrows. A curve and a straight line take the shortest path.

canvas_mark.description: The mark at one end of an arrow.

canvas_edge_animation.description: `flow` moves dashes and a dot along the arrow. `dash` moves only dashes, `dot` moves only a dot and `pulse` makes the arrow glow.

canvas_flow.description: The direction of the steps. `auto` puts them from left to right on a wide surface and from top to bottom on a narrow one.

canvas_pattern.description: The pattern on the background of the board.

board_issue_kind.description: The kind of an issue. A surface shows a mark for each kind.

board_priority.description: How soon an issue needs work, from highest to lowest.

limit.description: The most issues that the column should hold. A surface marks a column that holds more.

is_done.description: True when an issue in this column is done.

board_person.description: One person that an issue can name.

board_epic.description: One large piece of work that issues belong to.

board_issue.description: One issue of a board. An append with the id of an issue replaces that whole issue. Surfaces sort the issues of a column by `rank`, then by their order in the board.

key.description: The short name that people use for the issue, for example VIS-12.

column.description: The id of the column that holds the issue.

rank.description: The place of the issue in its column: a lower rank is higher in the column.

assignee.description: The id of the person who does the work. An id that `people` does not hold shows as the id.

epic.description: The id of the epic of the issue.

text.description: The description of the issue, as Markdown.

due.description: The date when the work must be done, as YYYY-MM-DD.

is_flagged.description: True when the issue is blocked or needs attention now.

updated_at.description: When the issue changed last, in milliseconds since 1970.

board_issue_change.description: The fields of an issue that a person sets. A field that is not given stays as it is. Null clears an optional field.
